performers: Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London; Artur Rodzinski, conductor
question: What changes when the opening’s sharp-edged gestures are enlarged into an orchestral mass?
intro: An angular exchange in the strings grows into a movement of long melodies, hard-driven development and a remarkably quiet ending. This is Rodzinski’s Westminster performance, credited on the LP to the Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London; the listening map follows this transfer, not a modern recording’s timings.

sections.label: Opening exchange
sections.mNote: Angular string gestures establish the opening material.

sections.label: Long lyrical span
sections.mNote: A quieter contrast; boundary is approximate.

sections.label: Developing drive
sections.mNote: Low-register activity begins a long accumulation.

sections.label: Orchestral crest
sections.mNote: Listening landmark, not an asserted recapitulation bar.

sections.label: Quiet recollection
sections.mNote: Lyrical material returns in a reduced texture.

sections.label: Closing suspension
sections.mNote: The last quiet span introduces the celesta colour.

cues.title: A divided argument
cues.text: Low and high strings answer one another with sharply profiled gestures. Listen to the space between the replies: this opening is an exchange, not yet a continuous melody supported by the whole orchestra.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 3, Moderato opening: cellos/basses and violins alternate; winds and brass rest. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: first 20 seconds contain the opening attack sequence. No individual bar alignment is claimed.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Less weight, more line
cues.text: The opening’s force subsides without stopping the music. Follow how a connected phrase can emerge from the same string-dominated sound, rather than waiting for a new instrumental colour to announce every change.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: five-second relative-level windows fall from −8.8 dB at 0:10 to −18.9 at 0:45; the score’s opening string span supplies the instrumental context (https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 3–9).

cues.title: An attack in print
cues.text: On 28 January 1936, Pravda attacked Shostakovich’s opera Lady Macbeth of Mtsensk in the article usually translated as “Muddle Instead of Music.” The Fifth followed in 1937. That chronology is documented; it does not turn each musical gesture into a coded political statement.
cues.evidence: Museum collection catalogue, surviving Pravda clipping, 28 January 1936: https://collectiononline.gctm.ru/entity/OBJECT/3028310 . Work chronology: https://shostakovich-en.ru/140en . Context cue, not a timed programmatic identification.

cues.title: A line finds support
cues.text: The lyrical writing still belongs to the opening region. Listen for winds and strings exchanging and supporting phrases rather than treating each new colour as a new section. The accompaniment can keep the line moving without becoming its foreground.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 4–7: earlier lyrical wind-and-string exchanges; the later harp-supported second-subject texture is not claimed here. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the 2:00–2:30 span varies markedly in level, before the quieter region after approximately 3:00. Placement is proportional, not a claim about a particular bar at 2:00.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A crest before retreat
cues.text: This is a local surge, not the movement’s largest climax. Keep its scale in mind: the next broad withdrawal will make the later orchestral accumulation feel much larger.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: level reaches −7.0 dB at 2:50, then falls through −15.5 at 3:00 to −22.4 at 3:15. The later maximum is −3.1 at 9:10.

cues.title: The quieter second world
cues.text: The long lyrical region gives the melody room to unfold over a much less forceful background. Attend to continuity rather than isolated accents: the tension now comes from how long a line can remain suspended.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, first-movement lyrical span, printed pp. 8–12; no exact second-subject entrance is assigned. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the sustained quiet region runs approximately 3:15–5:10, mostly around −19 to −23 dB.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A premiere in Leningrad
cues.text: Yevgeny Mravinsky conducted the first performance on 21 November 1937 in the Great Hall of the Leningrad Philharmonic. Rodzinski’s recording belongs to the work’s later international life, not to that premiere.
cues.evidence: https://shostakovich-en.ru/140en, premiere entry: Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra, Mravinsky, 21 November 1937. The Westminster sleeve identifies Rodzinski and the London orchestra: https://archive.org/download/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony.pdf .

cues.title: Quiet is not empty
cues.text: The low dynamic level lasts long enough to become a structural fact. Follow the small movements inside it; a quiet stretch can prepare a change without either a silence or a sudden new theme.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: windows from 4:20 through 5:10 remain near −19 to −23 dB, before the pronounced change around 5:10–5:22.

cues.title: Weight moves downward
cues.text: The piano and low strings help shift the argument into a harder-edged register. In the score this region makes accompaniment sound active and consequential: the engine underneath the melody begins to demand attention.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 12–13, rehearsal 17 and following: piano with low strings, then horns. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: strong boundaries at 5:10 and 5:22; relative level changes from −16.7 at 5:15 to −9.8 at 5:20, with a large spectral change. Instrument assignment is score-proportional, not machine instrument detection.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: An accumulation, not a leap
cues.text: Do not expect the development to stay loud once it has begun. It withdraws and gathers again. Listen for the persistence of motion through these changes of weight.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: after the 5:20 peak, levels retreat to −19.5 to −21.6 during 5:50–6:15, before rising again from 6:20.

cues.title: More bodies in motion
cues.text: The developing span enlarges the sound through overlapping orchestral layers. Try following the moving figures separately from the longer held or accented notes: density and loudness are related here, but they are not the same thing.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, development scoring, printed pp. 16–34: moving winds/strings against brass and other sustained or accented parts. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: levels rise from −16.1 at 6:20 toward −10.3 at 7:00. This is a broad passage assignment.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Applause had witnesses
cues.text: Maximilian Steinberg’s diary records an exceptional ovation at the premiere. Another witness, Lyubov Yakovleva, understood the applause as an answer to Shostakovich’s persecution. These are valuable individual accounts, not proof that every listener heard the same political message.
cues.evidence: https://shostakovich-en.ru/140en, contemporary diary accounts of the premiere, including Steinberg and Yakovleva. The cue distinguishes reported reception from a claim about the music’s hidden meaning.

cues.title: Pressure over a plateau
cues.text: The build now sustains its weight across several phrases. Listen beyond the nearest accent: the larger effect comes from remaining in this crowded, forceful sound instead of immediately releasing it.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: levels remain broadly around −6 to −8 dB from 8:20 to 8:45, with repeated onset activity; they rise further around 8:50–9:10.

cues.title: Towards the largest crest
cues.text: The movement is approaching its strongest measured peak in this transfer. Compare the mass of this sound with the bare string exchange at the beginning; the difference is one of scale as much as volume.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: −5.4 dB at 8:50, −5.3 at 9:05 and the loudest five-second window, −3.1, at 9:10. These are relative transfer levels, not score dynamic markings.

cues.title: A broad orchestral answer
cues.text: The score broadens the material into heavily supported orchestral statements. Hear how a gesture that once sounded like an interruption can acquire the weight of a proclamation when its register and accompaniment expand.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, first-movement broad climactic writing, printed pp. 34–43, including the Largamente region. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the peak near 9:10 is followed by a sustained, forceful span rather than an immediate return to the earlier quiet level. No precise recapitulation bar is asserted.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The crest has an afterlife
cues.text: The principal peak has passed, but the movement does not simply collapse. Follow the remaining waves of sound: an arrival can occupy a region, not just one decisive chord.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: the 9:25–10:45 windows remain broadly between −6 and −10 dB; a further local crest reaches −5.5 at 10:45.

cues.title: A dated Westminster object
cues.text: The source LP’s sleeve bears a 1956 Westminster copyright; its labels say WN 18001, while the sleeve says XWN 18001. Those are publication and catalogue facts. They do not establish that the orchestra recorded the music in 1956.
cues.evidence: Original sleeve and both labels, PDF pp. 2–4: https://archive.org/download/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony.pdf . Reissue session documentation is separately assessed in the dossier.

cues.title: Melody without the mass
cues.text: The lyrical material is recoloured by a much smaller group. In this late region, flute and horn can carry the line above light string motion; the earlier orchestral weight is no longer needed to make the phrase audible.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed p. 46, rehearsal 39: flute and horn lines, harp and quiet repeated strings. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 11:02 and level withdrawal from −10.4 at 10:50 to approximately −22 at 11:00–11:05. This aligns the reduced region only approximately.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A second kind of intensity
cues.text: The very soft sound asks for a different scale of attention. Listen for the shape of the line and the gaps around it, rather than expecting the ending to compete with the central climax.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: level reaches −26.4 at 12:00 and −27.0 at 12:05, far below the central crest. No specific instrument entrance is pinned to this cue.

cues.title: One last disturbance
cues.text: A brief swell interrupts the prolonged quiet, then retreats even farther. The ending has not yet become a simple fade: one local event can still change the balance of the whole quiet region.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 12:42; level rises from −27.5 at 12:40 to −10.8 at 12:50, then falls to −31.9 at 13:05. This describes the measured swell, not a bar-specific thematic identification.

cues.title: The smallest remaining colours
cues.text: The closing pages bring together solo violin, harp and, finally, celesta. Listen for the distinction between a bowed line and the short, bright attack of a keyboard or plucked string: the coda changes colour without rebuilding the earlier mass.
cues.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, printed pp. 50–51, rehearsals 44–47: solo violin, harp, muted strings/horns and the late celesta figures. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 13:30 marks a late quiet change. The cue covers the closing passage, not an exact celesta entrance.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Let the ending diminish
cues.text: The final span withdraws rather than offering another full orchestral answer. Let the resonance and the transfer’s residual noise remain distinct in your hearing; the end of a file is not necessarily the instant the last note is released.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: levels fall from about −24 dB at 14:00–14:15 to −29.4 at 14:20 and −33.2 at 14:25; decoded duration 874.7 seconds. No exact note-release timestamp is asserted.

transitions.title: A surge opens into space
transitions.how: The preceding swell gives way to a sustained lower level. The score’s longer string line and lighter accompaniment make the contrast by changing texture and scale, rather than requiring a complete stop. The marker names a region, not a proved bar boundary.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 8–12. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: −7.0 dB at 2:50, −15.5 at 3:00, −22.4 at 3:15.

transitions.title: The accompaniment acquires weight
transitions.how: A low-register, more sharply articulated texture emerges from the quiet lyrical span. Piano, low strings and then horns help turn accompaniment into a driving layer. The recorded change is strong, but its exact score bar is not established.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 12–13, rehearsal 17 and following. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundaries at 5:10 and 5:22, with level and spectral changes.

transitions.title: Accumulation becomes a broad crest
transitions.how: The developmental accumulation becomes a broad, heavily supported orchestral region. Increasing weight and sustained sonority carry the join; this landmark does not claim to identify the exact beginning of the recapitulation.
transitions.evidence: cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: increasing levels at 8:50–9:10 and maximum at 9:10. Broad scoring context: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 34–43.

transitions.title: The mass falls away
transitions.how: The forceful region releases its weight abruptly. A reduced lyrical texture can now be heard against light accompaniment; the flute-and-horn writing in the score offers a radically smaller answer to the preceding orchestral mass.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, p. 46, rehearsal 39. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: level falls from −5.5 at 10:45 to −22.2 at 11:00; boundary at 11:02.

transitions.title: Quiet sound changes its colour
transitions.how: The final quiet region changes instrumentation rather than restarting the argument. Harp, solo violin and the late celesta figures bring distinct attacks into a mostly sustained texture. This is a passage-level coda marker, not the exact first celesta note.
transitions.evidence: https://imslp.tw/uploads/PMLASIA01319-Shostakovich_Fifth_Symphony%2C__Op__47_-_Full_Score.pdf, pp. 50–51, rehearsals 44–47. cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony: boundary at 13:30; quiet levels continue to the end.

source.title: Symphony No. 5 — Muzgiz M. 16313 Г, historical full score
source.locator: Printed pp. 3–51; PDF pp. 5–53. Viewed historical score, hosted as public domain in Taiwan, not cleared for EU/US republication. Exact performing edition unknown. Selected passage snapshots, not a complete instrument-on/off transcription; approximate times use cache/analysis/shostakovich-5-moderato.txt; source: https://archive.org/details/lp_symphony-no-5-opus-47_dmitri-shostakovich-philharmonic-symphony.

timeline.note: Opening exchange across low and high strings; p. 3. A passage snapshot includes successive replies, not simultaneous playing on the first attack.

Long violin line over patterned lower strings and harp, pp. 8–10/rehearsal 9 and following; proportional placement within the quieter B span, supported by the report’s sustained low levels after 3:15.
Low-register development texture, pp. 12–13; report boundaries at 5:10/5:22 support the regional marker, not an exact horn entrance.
Broad orchestral crest, pp. 34–43; sustained loud region near 9:00–10:45. Snapshot omits instruments whose individual entries are not timed.
Reduced flute-and-horn lyrical texture, p. 46/rehearsal 39; approximately after the measured withdrawal near 11:00.
Closing solo-violin/harp and muted-string region, pp. 50–51; solo violin remains represented within violins-1.
Late celesta figures and quiet supporting parts, p. 51/rehearsal 47. Approximate closing-page snapshot, not an exact entry claim.

fields.label: Performers
fields.value: Philharmonic Symphony Orchestra of London (orchestra), Artur Rodzinski (conductor)
fields.note: Original sleeve and labels establish the displayed credit. Later Westminster reissue documentation and the publisher’s discography identify the orchestra as the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. That cross-identification is not substituted silently for the original label credit; individual players and soloists are not established.

fields.label: Work version
fields.note: The work and movement are identified, but the exact performing edition is not. The historical score supports broad orchestration and formal observations, not a claim of bar-exact agreement with Rodzinski’s materials. The movement is the entire supplied source track; no local audio edit is made. The set’s finale has a separately disclosed reported cut.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: CiNii’s record for Westminster MVCW-18008 explicitly gives this range; the publisher independently lists the Rodzinski/Royal Philharmonic recording as 1954. Applying those reissue data to this differently credited LP is an inference. No original session ledger or precise movement-by-movement day has been located. 1956 is the selected LP’s publication year, not an invented session date.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: Venue transcribed exactly from the reissue catalogue record. The original LP does not supply a venue. Its linkage to the selected LP is the same qualified inference as the session-date attribution; no more specific hall name is invented.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Not cleared as public domain in the EU or US; composition rights remain separate from the historic recording basis
fields.note: Shostakovich died in 1975. The ordinary EU life-plus-70 calculation runs through 2045; this is not a global clearance or a statement of a US expiry date. IMSLP identifies the work as non-public-domain in the EU and US. The inspected score is territorially hosted as public domain in Taiwan and is cited, not republished. No composition licence is asserted.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.value: Rule 3: territorial EU historic-recording basis; commercial circulation documented by December 1955, selected LP issue dated 1956
fields.note: The original Westminster sleeve/labels and album metadata establish the selected 1956 WN 18001/XWN 18001 issue. A visually inspected High Fidelity review, December 1955, p. 80, already names this London orchestra, Rodzinski, his second recording of the Fifth and Westminster catalogue 18001; the review prints SWN 18001 and erroneously calls the symphony D major, so those details are not silently normalized. The publisher also lists Nixa WLP 20004 in 1955. First lawful publication anywhere before 1963 is the rule; no EU-first-release claim is required or made. source.rights.published 1956 remains a conservative upper bound tied to the selected physical issue, not a first-release date. Even using 1956, the ordinary 50-year recording term had expired before the 2013 extension. US sound-recording status is not established. Complete item metadata, original side-transfer provenance and scans disclose no Creative Commons non-commercial condition or separate upstream digital source. This is not a worldwide public-domain or composition-rights clearance.

composer.epithet: Fifteen symphonies and fifteen quartets turn marches, fugues and a four-note signature into arguments about public ceremony and individual memory.
facts: Petrograd Conservatory from 1919: piano with Leonid Nikolayev, composition with Maximilian Steinberg
Leningrad Conservatory from 1937; Moscow Conservatory from 1943; dismissed from both in 1948
DSCH = D–E♭–C–B, using German note names
Fifteen symphonies · fifteen string quartets · six concertos · operas, songs and film scores
composer.background:
Dmitri Shostakovich was born in St Petersburg in 1906, the son of an engineer and a pianist. His mother, Sofiya, gave him his first piano lessons; in 1919 he entered the Petrograd Conservatory, where Leonid Nikolayev taught him piano and Maximilian Steinberg composition. The director, Alexander Glazunov, supported the young musician through the shortages following revolution and civil war. His father’s death in 1922 worsened the family’s finances, and Shostakovich earned money accompanying silent films. He graduated in piano in 1923 and composition in 1925: the graduation score was his First Symphony, written before his nineteenth birthday.

Nikolai Malko conducted its première in Leningrad on 12 May 1926. The orchestra includes a piano, whose abrupt interventions contribute to the symphonic argument. Clarinet, bassoon and trumpet exchange short phrases; a waltz can become a march without a change of personnel. International performances followed. Shostakovich still considered a performing career and received an honourable mention at the first Warsaw Chopin Competition in 1927. Thereafter his public piano appearances increasingly centred on his own works, including the concertos, chamber music and songs.
